date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 20) titled "Glory 1 July 3rd"; the text calls itself the first edition of Glory in this run, and 3 July 2002 was a Wednesday, the weekday of the run's Glory shows

Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 19) titled "Glory 2 July 10th"; the text opens "WELCOME TO THE SECOND EDITION OF FIVE STAR WRESTLING WEDNESDAY NIGHT GLORY"

Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 18) titled "Glory 3 July 17th"; the text is the third Glory (it follows the 10 July show's tape-and-chair story)

name: Glory 4

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 17) titled "Glory 4 July 24th"; the text opens "WELCOME TO THE 4TH EDITION OF FIVE STAR WRESTLING GLORY"

notes: The Jason O'Neil v Tyler Davidson match ends when Angelo Deville and Chris Bagwell run in and the referee "calls for the bell"; the commentary says the referee "has just thrown this match out", but the text never rules a result, so the row carries none.

name: Glory 5

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 16) titled "Glory 5 July 31st"; the text carries the Timo Bolamba v Mike Marvelous main event that the 24 July show announced for "next week"

notes: The four corners match ends "Winner: No Contest" (Michel Krieg, a run-in, helps Ming with a chair); the row carries that declared outcome. The Timo Bolamba v Mike Marvelous main event ends with both men pinned at once and each referee raising a different hand; the text never rules it. The row carries the draw the fed itself declared in its next show (7 August: the CEO says the tape was reviewed and "they have all unanimously agreed that it was a draw").

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 15) titled "Glory 6 Aug 7th"; the text opens on the hotel scene the 31 July closet gag set up and recaps that show's gauntlet

name: Glory 7

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 14) titled "Glory 7 Aug 14th"; the text calls itself "THE LAST EDITION OF GLORY BEFORE FSW GENESIS", and Genesis is dated 18 August

notes: The text's own opening names the Jacksonville Coliseum in Jacksonville, Florida; a later line has the crowd "here in Macon". The venue is the opening's (see SOURCES-DISAGREE-2002-A).

name: Genesis 2002

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 57, post 2) titled "Aug 18th"; the text is the "first pay-per-view since the rebirth, aptly titled Genesis", and the Glory shows before and after it name the date

matches.stipulation: number one Contendership of the FSW World Tag Team Titles
two out of three falls match

notes: The four-way for the vacant FSW World Championship is thrown out when the referee, after Mike Frampton's chair shots, rules a no contest ("THIS MATCH HAS BEEN RULED A NO CONTEST"); no champion is crowned. Ming and Michel Krieg win the FSW Tag Team Championship from A Tag Team and are challenged by Bad Frotitude straight afterwards (no ruling); Angelo Deville wins the Primetime Championship from Jason O'Neil.

name: Glory 8

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 13) titled "Glory 8 Aug 21st". The post's title says 21 August; the text says "A SPECIAL THURSDAY EDITION OF FSW GLORY" coming off Genesis (Sunday 18 August), and 22 August 2002 was the Thursday, so the booking date stands (the sources disagree by one day; see SOURCES-DISAGREE-2002-A)

notes: The FSW Tag Team Championship defence by Ming and Michel Krieg against Bad Frotitude is broken up by the masked bikers billed "DEAD PRESIDENTS" and is never finished; the text rules no result. Angelo Deville keeps the Primetime Championship by submission over John Jupiter.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 10) titled "Glory 11 Sept 11th"; the text is dedicated to "the lives lost in the attacks of September 11th, 2001" and calls itself a "special Thursday edition", though 11 September 2002 was a Wednesday (listed in SOURCES-DISAGREE)

Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 9) titled "Glory 12 Sept 26th"; the text opens "FSW Glory - 26th September 2002. Target Center, Minnesota, Minneapolis"

matches.stipulation: THERE ARE NO DQs, NO TIME LIMIT, NO COUNTOUTS, AND THERE MUST BE A WINNER

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 8) titled "Glory 13 Oct. 3rd"; the text opens "FSW Glory - 3rd October 2002. Kohl Center, Madison, Wisconsin"

Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 6) titled "Glory 15 Oct. 16th"; the text opens "FSW GLORY, OCTOBER 16th, 2002"; no venue is named (the opening strobe line says "the Target Center", a line repeated from the 26 September show)

name: Bad Moon Rising 2002

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 57, post 1) titled "Oct 18th, 2002", the write-up of the pay-per-view; the preceding Glory text announces it "October 20th, From The Salem State Apitheater, Salem Massachussettes" and the text itself says it is the "outdoor Salem Amphitheater"; 20 October 2002 was a Sunday, the day the following Glory texts call "Sunday" (the 15 October text's own reminder says "October 21": listed in SOURCES-DISAGREE)

notes: Kimbusa v Kyle Velocity (match 3 of the pay-per-view card, order 2) ends on a three count made by Steven Caldera himself, who has climbed into the ring while the referee lies unconscious; the row carries the fall as the build records it and no ruling by an official exists.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 5) titled "Glory 16 Oct. 30th"; the text names no date or venue (it opens on the closing minutes of the Bad Moon Rising text and runs "one week removed from the greatest event of our companies history"), so the date rests on the post title and the weekly Wednesday run

Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 4) titled "Glory 17 Nov 6th"; the text places the show at the Phillips Arena in Atlanta ("ATLANTA, GEORGIA!")

name: Glory 18

notes: The Alliances-team draw leaves the main event (order 7, the Untouchables against Mob Rule) without a ruling: the text ends on the beating of Timo Bolamba and Mike Marvelous before the bell is reported. The ten entrants are placed from the card as the build lists them; the row carries no result.

name: Glory 20

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, a post on its own News Publisher board (category 56, post 1) titled "Glory 20 Nov. 27th"; the text opens "Wednesday, November 27, 2002 / From Rupp Arena in Lexington, Kentucky"

notes: The triple threat (order 6) ends with Boda counting a pin on Six Finger Cisco himself after knocking out the referee; no official or announcer rules a winner, so the row carries no result. The tag match (order 4) is announced a double disqualification.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-04-08 and 2001-10-31), which dates a card called High Impact 8/27/00; the write-up itself carries no date line.

matches.note: Meanstreak won with a powerbomb.

matches.stipulation: four corner match, texas tornado match
matches.note: For the Lightweight title. Shelldog won with a jumping DDT on Suicide and became the new Lightweight champion.

matches.stipulation: Iron man tables match from hell
matches.note: For the Extreme title, with Killer Kactus as special referee and Red Hurricane as special enforcer; both were put down during it. Time expired with Dysan appearing to have sent Jacob Jackson through the last burning tables, but Mike Marvelous, wearing the referee's shirt, ruled that time had run out first and awarded the title to Jackson.

For the Rising Star title. The Bulldozer came out of a door in the backstage fight with a bat and then dropped Troy Rivers on the concrete; The Riddler covered Rivers and became the new Rising Star champion.

For the tag team titles. The X-Treme Demons were eliminated first and 2nd To None second; Shelldog ran in with a chair, Coma fell backwards into it, and The Ripper rolled him up so that The Psycho Brotherz became the new tag team champions.

For the Prime Time title, the first of that championship. Marvelous won and was announced the first FSW Prime Time champion; afterwards he wrapped the strap around Keeton's neck until officials pulled him off.

For the Intercontinental title, with Chris Remicho as special guest referee. Cyle Chaos won and was announced the first FSW Intercontinental champion; Epitome of Evil set Remicho on fire with a blowtorch during the match.
Painkiller won with a pinfall after an unidentified wrestler hit a bulldog on Static.
For the World title. Steve Johnson won two falls to one and became the new FSW World champion.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-04-08 and 2001-10-31), which dates a card called Total Annihellation 10/1/00; the write-up itself carries no date line.

matches.note: Ruled a no contest when Embankment, Aaron and Josh Banks, ran in and attacked both teams.
For the Rising Star title. Red Hurricane won with The Hurricane and became the new Rising Star champion.

For the Extreme title, inside a cell. A masked man dropped through the roof of the cell and attacked both men; Dysan came to the ring, took the Extreme title for the time being and had the result announced as a no decision.
For the Prime Time title, with Ms. Wynters at Marc North's side. North made Keeton tap to The Point Of No Return and became the new Prime Time champion.

For the Intercontinental title, which Big Davylicious held. Il Mito hit the referee with a chair and took the key; OnSlaught ordered the match restarted, and Big Davylicious was announced the winner and still champion.

For the FSW World Championship, with Eve at Epitome of Evil's side and Mike Marvelous at Jacob Jackson's. Jackson took the first fall with the Idolizer after Marvelous hit Epitome of Evil with a chair; Epitome of Evil levelled it by powerbombing Jackson through a flaming table; Razor Blade then ran in and hit the Razor Spike, leaving the referee, Jackson and Epitome of Evil down; Epitome of Evil got up first and won the deciding fall with the Hells Entrance Powerbomb to take the title.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-04-08 and 2001-10-31), which dates a card called Fallen 10/29/00; the write-up itself carries no date line.

matches.note: Holy Man won.
X-BaLL came to the ring, put the referee in the X-Clamat!on Po!nt, put on the referee's shirt and counted the pin on Jack Miller for Big Gooey Sac; he then attacked Miller with a chair.
X-BaLL won; Psycho, Black Cloud, Chad, Dagger, Crazy and Damian, named by the card, also fought in it, and X-BaLL, Mike Carter and Damian were the last three.
For the Extreme title, which Jimmy the Sniff held. Aggonizer won and became the new Extreme champion.

matches.stipulation: Hell In A Cell Ladder Match
matches.note: For the Rising Star title, which Cell held. Colin Baird escaped the cell, climbed the ladder on top of it and took the belt to become the new Rising Star champion; Cell fell through the announcers' table.
The winners were to be the number one contenders to the tag titles. The referee was knocked down during the match; Lance Klipped and Brian Ironside, Total Impact, won.
For the Prime Time title and X-Rated's FSW debut. Steve Johnson attacked X-Rated and Steve Jackson won, becoming the new Prime Time champion.
For the ICW and FSW Intercontinental titles. Big Daveylicious won.

For the number one contendership to the World title, billed as Creature against Jacob Jackson. Jackson took the first fall with a Rock Bottom; Creature won the second with a big elbow and the third with the Abyss. Earlier Steve Johnson had set Jackson's face on fire backstage, and the commentary afterwards suggests Johnson may have been the bandaged man in the ring.

For the World title, with Eve handcuffed in the top level of the cage and the title around her waist; the cage held four trash cans, one of them with the keys. Matthew Morrison won and became the new FSW World champion; Marc North attacked Epitome of Evil afterwards.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-04-08 and 2001-10-31), which dates a card called Final Destination 11/26/00; the write-up itself carries no date line.

matches.note: For the number one contendership to the Rising Star title. Tommy Tremonti, Jonathan Thompson, Brian Lawson and Shinigami Kishin also fought in it; Corey Phoenix pinned Brian Lawson and Jonathan Thompson, hit Shinigami Kishin with brass knuckles and then pinned him and Tommy Tremonti together to win.
Billed as Mike Carter against Stung One; Armageddon won, and a masked-figure promo of the new man followed.
The result was announced as a double disqualification.
For the Extreme title, which X-Ball held. Hardcore Camo won and became the new Extreme champion; Jack Miller afterwards ran him down in the parking lot and took the title.
Scott Knight dropped from the rafters and hit Scorpion with a lead pipe; Little Great One won with a frog splash from the top of the cage.
For the Prime Time title, which X-Rated held. Razor Blade helped X-Rated and Dragon helped Aggonizer; Aggonizer won and became the new Prime Time champion.
For the Rising Star title. Scott Knight won and stayed champion.
For the Intercontinental title. Jesse Gunn attacked both men; Colin Baird won and became the new Intercontinental champion.

The main event for the World title, with Marc North as special guest referee. The match broke up into a hunt through the backstage rooms; Creature found Big Daveylicious lying cut and motionless in a room with the World title on a table, picked the title up, and was announced the new champion. Marc North attacked him with a chair afterwards.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (DATE: 2/20/01); the fed's own February 2001 calendar (shows.thefsw.com/dates/february_2001.htm, captured 2001-03-05) lists the same Glory on the same day and in the same arena.

matches.note: The Ripper won with the Firestarter; afterwards The Reaper and Jack Miller ran in with chairs and the three beat Cage down.
Tommy Taker won with Instant Gratification.
Excaliber and Justin Mills won, with the pinfall on Rob Knight.

The two brawled through the arena and out to a loading dock; Epitome of Evil lifted Phoenyx for a powerbomb and went off the platform through two tables, and the broadcast cut away before any finish was shown.

Billed as Max Danger against Johnny Mayhem, who came out in street clothes on doctor's orders and sent Sound in his place. Jack Miller and the Psycho Brothers ran in, and Max Danger was awarded the match by disqualification before they beat him down.

Billed as Steve Johnson's last appearance in FSW. Epitome of Evil came to ringside and attacked both men, and Mike Marvelous then won with the Marvelocity. A masked man, introduced as Creature, stood in the ring afterwards.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (Date: February 26, 2001); the fed's own February 2001 calendar (shows.thefsw.com/dates/february_2001.htm, captured 2001-03-05) lists the same pay-per-view on the same day and in the same arena.

matches.note: Sean Rivers won with a sit-down piledriver, pinning The Legacy.
For the Lightweight title. Ron Jacobs won and became the new Lightweight champion.
For the Extreme title. Jack Miller won and became the new Extreme champion.
For the Rising Star title. Rob Knight jumped out of the crowd and clotheslined Excaliber from behind, then won and became the new Rising Star champion.
For the Prime Time title. Steve Jackson hit Anthony Brown, and Jimmy Smith won and became the new Prime Time champion.

For the tag team titles, billed as an elimination match: Aggonizer beat down his partner Dragon at the entrance and left, announcing that the match was now decided by the first pin. P.S. Mad covered Keith O'Neil while The Reaper pushed down on P.S. Mad to keep O'Neil from kicking out, and P.S. Mad and Sound became the new tag team champions.
For the Intercontinental title. Aggonizer won and became the new Intercontinental champion.

For the number one contendership to the World title, with no falls and no disqualifications. Ironfist, billed as not a wrestler, dropped from the rafters and kicked Johnny Mayhem off the ladder, then knocked the ladder into Lucky McKnight as he reached the top; Lucky McKnight grabbed the prize and landed on Mayhem.

For the FSW World Heavyweight Championship. Epitome of Evil entered after Marvelous and Onslaught had started, and the two teamed against Onslaught until Epitome of Evil turned on Marvelous. The returning Creature came out and brawled with Marvelous, then unmasked as Jacob Jackson; Phoenyx and Tommy Taker each attacked Epitome of Evil. Onslaught made Marvelous tap to Courage Required, then beat Epitome of Evil with the same hold, the referee ruling him out, to win the title.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (Date: March 25, 2001); the fed's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-10-31) dates its World title change to the same day.

matches.note: Matty won with a moonsault in a match added to the card shortly before the show.

The winner was to meet neXt for the Rising Star title. Jason Winters knocked down the referee by accident while celebrating; neXt ran in and hit Winters with the neXt boMb, and S. Sterling Silver covered him for the three.
Chris Taylor won.
For the tag team titles, a handicap match against the champion P.S. Mad. P.S. Mad won and stayed champion.
For the Rising Star title. neXt won and stayed champion.

If Epitome of Evil won he would meet Painkiller in a steel cage. Tommy Taker nearly won with a DDT; Razor Blade then hit Taker with the Razor Spike, and Epitome of Evil finished with the Three Drills To Hell.
For the Prime Time title. Sean Rivers won with the Rivernator and stayed champion.
For the Intercontinental title, which Johnny Mayhem held; Carlton Carter joined the match. Mayhem pinned Carter and stayed champion.
For the vacant World title. Mike Marvelous won and became the new World champion.

For the Extreme title, which Jack Miller held; the card bills “Punisher 2000 vs. Jack Miller vs. Shawn Davies vs. Aggonizer” and the write-up calls two of them Punisher and Steve Davies. The match began backstage and ran through the arena; Miller piledrove Punisher through a table from the top of a ladder, then pinned Aggonizer after a brainbuster and stayed champion.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (DATE: 4/6/01); the fed's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-10-31) dates two title rows to the same day, and its April 2001 calendar (shows.thefsw.com/dates/april_2001.htm, captured 2001-03-05) lists the same Maximum Velocity on the same day, naming a different arena.

matches.note: For the FSW Extreme Championship. Shawn Davies won the title with a frog splash from a ten-foot ladder through a table.
For the Rising Star title, ruled a no contest when Lance Klipped ran in and attacked neXt; Christian Diablo then came in and superkicked Sterling Silver.
P.S. Mad won with a moonsault.
For the Prime Time title. Sean Rivers made Suicide submit and stayed champion.
Carlton Carter won after Big Daveylicious interfered.

Epitome of Evil twice hit Tommy Taker with a chair at Taker's own invitation; Big Daveylicious then ran in and hit Epitome of Evil with it, and Taker pinned him. Epitome of Evil afterwards hit Big Daveylicious and then Taker with the ring bell and powerbombed Taker through a table.

Billed as Marvelous and Johnny Mayhem against Tommy Taker and Big Daveylicious; Taker, hurt in the match before, was replaced by Carlton Carter. With Painkiller at ringside and both chairs used on Marvelous, Carter pinned him.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, whose second and third parts carry the date line DATE: 4/10/01; the fed's own April 2001 calendar (shows.thefsw.com/dates/april_2001.htm, captured 2001-03-05) lists the same Glory on the same day in the same arena. Part 1 reads DATE: 4/20/01, a disagreement filed with the page record.

matches.note: Tony Barrera won with Game Over.
Andy Overdose won.
MVP Tyrone Williams won with a cradle piledriver.
Sabin Green wrestled in Shawn Davies' place, and Davies and Stan Phear helped him; Green's pinfall won it for Davies' side.
The winner was to be the number one contender to the Rising Star title. S. Sterling Silver won with The Tarnisher.

For the Prime Time title. Carlton Carter and Tommy Taker ran in, Carter broke a champagne bottle over Rivers and the referee counted three for Big Daveylicious; Jacob Jackson, as vice president, reversed the decision on screen and ruled Sean Rivers the winner by disqualification, still champion.
Big Daveylicious and Tommy Taker interfered and knocked out the referee; Epitome of Evil ran in, Johnny Mayhem hit Carter with the Fatal Error, and Epitome of Evil counted the fall himself.
The World champion Mike Marvelous lost to Tommy Taker, who hit him with a chair and a kendo stick after the referee had been knocked out and then won with the referee revived.
Painkiller's job and a World title shot were at stake. Epitome of Evil won with the Three Drills To Hell; Tommy Taker, Eve, Johnny Mayhem and Chris Taylor all took part.
For the number one contendership to the Extreme title. The write-up bills him Aggonier (once Aggoinizer). Punisher 2000 won with a Punished DDT from the turnbuckle through three flaming tables.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (Date: April 29, 2001); the fed's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-10-31) dates six rows to the same day.

matches.note: The opening match of the show, not on the announced card. Ferrari Jones won with a German suplex.
The first Alley Match in FSW. MVP won with the Most Valuable Move through a dumpster.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, which carries its own date line (Date: May 27, 2001); the fed's own title history (thefsw.com/history/titlehistory.shtml, captured 2001-10-31) and the show's own preview page (ppvs.thefsw.com/foreigndisaster/index.shtml, captured 2001-06-02) give the same day.

matches.note: The first match of the World title round robin. Big Daveylicious kicked Epitome of Evil low while the referee was occupied, then pinned him with the Daveylicious Bomb as Epitome of Evil set up the Three Drills To Hell.
LSD won.
Christian Diablo won with a moonsault, with Mike Extreme at ringside.
Tyler Cash won with a dragon rana from the top of the cage.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own write-up of the show, whose title line reads Futile Resistance: 11.03.2001 and whose segment heading reads [November 3rd]; the fed's fan column dated 11.10.2001 calls it this past Sunday (4 November), a disagreement filed with the page record.

matches.note: For the tag team titles. Human pinned Atrius and kept the titles.
For the Extreme and Rising Star titles. P.S. Mad won with the Psycho Driver and took both titles.
For the World title; it began as Chris Fear against Stefan Douglas and became a three-way with Blitz. Blitz won with Heavy Artillery on Chris Fear and became the new World champion.
For the Intercontinental title, which Punisher 2000 held. Chris Fear came over the barricade and held Tommy Taker by the ankle while Jonny Trip climbed and pulled the title down to become champion.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own record, dated jointly with Argyle's side (the date of the fed's own write-up of the show).

matches.note: Boda against Timo Bolamba with Mike Marvelous as special guest referee. Marvelous crotched Bolamba on the top rope and speared him, then put Boda in the MARVELock as Boda covered, counted three himself and announced himself the winner; the text gives the match no other result.

date.source: Five Star Wrestling's own record, dated jointly with Argyle's side (the date of the fed's own write-up of the show).
